rows.recommendation: Pull TA_Festival_Push_App off Meta and find out why 1 in 5 rupees comes back as a refund
rows.source_table: Refund rate by campaign — transactions joined to users.utm_campaign
rows.value_if_works: ≈ ₹9.2L recovered over 6 months, or ≈ ₹1.6L/month spend avoided if the campaign is paused
rows.arithmetic: At the other campaigns' 3.59% value-weighted refund rate, expected refunds are ≈ ₹2.13L versus ₹11.3L actual.
rows.condition: The spike is driven by this campaign's audience or promise and is fixable, rather than random noise.
rows.assumption: Refund reasons are not in the export, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.

rows.recommendation: Shift ad budget out of TA_Generic_Astro_Wide into TA_Love_Retarget_Web
rows.number: ₹418.70 CAC/payer for Astro Wide versus ₹296.62 for Love Retarget Web
rows.source_table: Meta spend divided by distinct successful payers from transactions joined to users
rows.value_if_works: ≈ 95 additional paying users on the same ₹96,300 budget
rows.arithmetic: ₹96,300 ÷ ₹296.62 ≈ 325 payers versus 230 today. The illustrative revenue read-through is ≈ ₹25L.
rows.condition: Love's marginal efficiency holds without saturating its smaller retargeting audience.
rows.assumption: The revenue scenario assumes the observed tier mix holds; it is not a forecast.

rows.recommendation: Investigate why Android converts at 5.87% against iOS's 9.82%
rows.number: 1,539-payer gap if Android reached iOS's rate
rows.source_table: Paid conversion by device — users.device joined to transactions
rows.value_if_works: Closing one third of the gap would add roughly 500 paying users
rows.condition: The gap is caused by a fixable Android experience issue such as checkout friction or payment support.
rows.assumption: Campaign mix is similar across devices, but other confounders remain. Audit before acting.
